The consumer

Being “Mufat” is the new normal.

This generation cares more about details and uniqueness. They are expressive, self-aware, ziddi, argumentative, with attention to detail and a main character aura. They speak about everything, and everything they own speaks about them.

01

He has opinions now

Especially the modern Indian man, who surprisingly now has opinions. He has identities. He is becoming more conscious of taste.

02

The wardrobe became a runway

Gone are the days where the wardrobe looked like a shelf. Now it is a whole runway, where he chooses how he would like to be seen, and chooses a look.

03

Culturally plugged in

More fashion aware, more experimental, and moving steadily from utility to taste to identity.

THE CONSUMER03
The behaviour, in reported numbers

People aren't just shopping fashion.
They're consuming taste.

What Myntra is saying

Its CEO says Gen Z fashion purchase frequency runs 30 to 40% higher than millennials, that Gen Z wants full-look styling rather than isolated catalogue shots, and that footwear and accessories are growing ahead of the market. Creator-led shopping already contributes around 10% of Myntra revenue.

What Deloitte is saying

Around 40% of consumers tried new fashion brands in the prior year, driven by recommendations, social influence and accessible price points, alongside a shift toward intentional, quality and experience led consumption.

PROOF OF CONCEPT06
Is the market catching up? · 01 of 05

The emerging consumer problem is taste discovery.

He is not short of product. He is short of a way to work out which product is him. Every signal in the research points at the same missing layer: somebody to organise taste on his behalf.

What that makes the job

Not a bigger catalogue. A shorter distance between seeing something and knowing it is yours.

Mind map, visual identity and consumer drivers
THE MARKET07
Is the market catching up? · 02 of 05

Legacy brands don't cater to the new generation.

When you enter a mall, don't all the stores look the same?

> 30 yrs

Their average customer age keeps rising, and the assortment rises with it.

Untouched themes

Brutalist fashion, plain and simple but unique in form. Modern art deco. Disagreement curation. Resilience. Stubborn anti pressure.

No experimentation

Nor do they experiment with fabrics, silhouettes, colours or forms. The shelf has not moved in a decade.

The gap it leaves

A generation that treats clothing as argument is being sold to by brands that treat it as inventory.

THE MARKET08
Is the market catching up? · 03 of 05

Rigid brand language.

Ever wondered how trend setting houses like Dior, Versace and Chanel never die? Because they have a flexible and timeless brand DNA. Indian accessory brands have neither.

01

Occasion based brands barely exist

There is no distinctive accessory proposition built around college, weekends, nightlife, dates, festivals or social occasions.

02

New age brands solve functional occasions

Work, commute and travel dominate the category, while the much larger world of self expression and social occasions stays underserved.

THE MARKET09
Is the market catching up? · 04 of 05

Taste at an accessible price.

Consumers are developing premium taste faster than the market is giving them accessible products that reflect that taste. Even with options in front of him, the question stays: what goes with me?

Evidence wall, each one proves he pays for design first elsewhere
What 635 scraped reviews say

Design is the strongest positive theme in the category. When consumers get it, they reward it. Durability rates highest when it shows up, but design is what gets mentioned unprompted.

THE MARKET10
Is the market catching up? · 05 of 05

The internet is solving taste.
Discovery is still broken.

7 lakh
commerce creators on Instagram above 10K followers
50% CAGR
male commerce creators, twice the female rate

Fashion is 50% of that pool, beauty 35%, home 15%, growing at roughly 25% overall. Of the 7 lakh, about 30% are male, so 2.1 lakh, and compounding fastest. Money is flowing across apparel and non apparel alike.

Reels routinely run on comment LINK, comment SHOP and DM for links, with some generating hundreds of thousands to millions of views.

RUMOAR12
Starting with accessories

Because you don't need a new wardrobe to become a new version of yourself.

The glow-up ladder

He upgraded everything except what he carries.

Where the category currently sits

Accessories are an add on for fashion houses, or parked with luggage players for carry, opticians for sunglasses, legacy players for watches and marketplaces for jewellery. Nobody owns it as a whole.

A complete look, bag, eyewear, cap, watch, jewellery and shoes, means six brands and six separate shopping journeys. The market organises accessories by category. The consumer is left to assemble an identity on their own.
